Corporate Strategy is Kenneth Richmond Andrews's; Protest Diffusion is Kenneth T. Andrews's with Biggs; the Saskatchewan thesis is Kenneth David Andrews's.

Page's (3/9). Where the loony bin is remains unverified, leaving the key share around 0.56-0.67 and dominance uncertain. The zero-weight Fauvisme catalogue belongs to Suzanne Pagé.

The astronomy books and Victorian essays are Richard Anthony Proctor's, approximately 14/15 listed citation weight; The Influence of Food on Civilization dates to 1882 despite the supplied 1916. The Anti-Tobacco Campaign of the Nazis (1996) is Robert N. Proctor's, explicitly credited by the journal and PubMed (1/15).

Death by Government (weight 2), Democracy, Power, Genocide, and Mass Murder, China's Bloody Century and Libertarianism and International Violence are R. J. Rummel's (5/6). The Importance of Being Doctor, Catholic Historical Review 82 (1996), 187-203, is Erika Rummel's (1/6), as the journal's contents confirm.

The Lake Superior report (weight 2) and Metallic Wealth are Josiah Dwight Whitney's (3/6), an even split. The Cambridge Medieval History and The Late Professor J. B. Bury are James Pounder Whitney's (2/6); the garbled Guild Books entry is Janet Whitney's Elizabeth Fry (1/6). The second geological report has zero weight.

Presidential Decision Making Adrift is David Wells Engstrom's and carries four citations. The Lost Origins of American Fair Employment Law (2011), carrying one citation, explicitly names David Freeman Engstrom on the Stanford Law Review title page. Thus the key accounts for 4/5 listed citation weight.
